---
title: "Git and GitHub cheat sheet"
---

## One-time setup

```bash
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
```

## Start a project

| Task | Command line | GitHub Desktop |
|---|---|---|
| New repo in the current folder | `git init` | File → New repository |
| Copy a repo from GitHub | `git clone <url>` | File → Clone repository |
| Connect a local repo to GitHub | `git remote add origin <url>` | Publish repository |

## Everyday loop

| Task | Command line | GitHub Desktop |
|---|---|---|
| Get the latest changes | `git pull` | Fetch / Pull origin |
| See what changed | `git status`, `git diff` | Changes tab |
| Stage files | `git add <file>` or `git add .` | Check the files |
| Commit | `git commit -m "Message"` | Summary → Commit |
| Send to GitHub | `git push` | Push origin |
| View history | `git log --oneline` | History tab |

## Branches

| Task | Command line | GitHub Desktop |
|---|---|---|
| List branches | `git branch` | Current branch ▾ |
| Create and switch | `git switch -c name` | New branch |
| Switch | `git switch name` | Current branch ▾ → choose |
| Push a new branch | `git push -u origin name` | Publish branch |
| Delete a local branch | `git branch -d name` | Branch → Delete |
| Open a pull request | (on github.com) | Create Pull Request |

## Undo

| Task | Command line | GitHub Desktop |
|---|---|---|
| Discard edits to a file | `git restore <file>` | Right-click → Discard changes |
| Unstage a file | `git restore --staged <file>` | Uncheck the file |
| Undo the last commit (not pushed) | `git reset --soft HEAD~1` | History → Undo commit |
| Reverse a pushed commit | `git revert <id>` | History → Revert changes in commit |
| Stop tracking a file | `git rm --cached <file>` | n/a |

## Before every push

- [ ] Checked every changed file
- [ ] No data, PHI, or PII
- [ ] No passwords, tokens, keys, or server names
- [ ] `.gitignore` is up to date

## Something sensitive got pushed?

1. **Revoke or change** any exposed secret immediately.
2. Tell an owner: Max Wegener ([mwegener@health.nv.gov](mailto:mwegener@health.nv.gov)) or Jordan Lancaster ([jlancaster@health.nv.gov](mailto:jlancaster@health.nv.gov)).
3. For PHI or PII, follow the agency's incident reporting procedures.
